title: End-to-end pipeline runbook
context: By end of M1, the pipeline has six moving parts: allow-list, taxonomy, schema/CI, style guide, review rubric, and automated checks. A new contributor (human or agent) pulling a QPL authoring task needs to understand the full end-to-end sequence — what to do, in what order, with which artifacts — without reading every plan document. The runbook is the single authoritative how-to reference for authoring and shipping a QPL set. It also defines the maintenance cycle (re-review cadence, source-drift response) and the de-listing procedure.
objective: Write docs/runbook.md — a step-by-step end-to-end pipeline runbook covering: (1) selecting a topic x stage cell; (2) verifying and using allow-listed sources; (3) authoring original questions per the style guide with UNCERTAIN: flags; (4) running local CI checks before PR; (5) handing off to reviewers using the reviewer-handoff template; (6) resolving UNCERTAIN: flags and reviewer feedback; (7) final CI gates before merge; (8) maintenance cycle (nextReviewDue, source-drift response, withdrawal procedure).
acceptanceCriteria: docs/runbook.md covers all 8 pipeline stages listed in the objective, in order, with enough specificity that a first-time contributor can execute each step without reading PLAN.md

The runbook references the correct artifact path for each tool: sources/allow-list.yaml, taxonomy/ files, templates/style-guide.md, templates/review-rubric.md, templates/reviewer-handoff.md, support/resources.yaml, scripts/ checks
The runbook includes the commands to run local CI checks (pnpm test and the relevant scripts) and what a passing vs failing output looks like

The runbook includes a Maintenance cycle section explaining: checking nextReviewDue, responding to source-drift alerts from the watcher, and the withdrawal-or-re-review procedure when a source license or clinical guideline changes
The runbook is concise (under 2500 words), written in plain language, and is itself consistent with the style guide it references
Maintainer has reviewed and approved the runbook before merge
resources: PLAN.md (Solution approach — Pipeline; Quality gates; Sustainability)
